title: Kashmir Shaivism opening (the Shiva Sutras)
hook: a two-word line in the Shiva Sutras says the teacher is the way, and a hand guiding a hand shows what that means

segments.voice: Yesterday in Kashmir Shaivism opening, the Shiva Sutras built a theater: the self a dancer, the inner self the stage, the senses the audience. Did you catch yourself walking onstage? Day one thousand one hundred forty-three.
screen: `THE SELF IS A DANCER.` · `TODAY: THE TEACHER.`

segments.voice: A grandmother's hand closes over a child's hand on a slate. Together they draw the first letter, slowly, the curve and then the line. The child couldn't have found that shape alone. And nobody hands the letter over like a coin. The small hand just moves with the bigger one until it knows the way. The Shiva Sutras have a line about that kind of passing on, and it's two words long. Gurur upayah. The teacher is the way. Today, the person who walks beside the path.
screen: `A HAND OVER A HAND.` → `THE FIRST LETTER.` → `GURUR UPAYAH.`

segments.voice: Guru is a teacher. Upaya is a means, a way, the method that gets you somewhere. Put together: the teacher is the means. It's easy to read past, because it's so short. But think about what this book has said so far. Consciousness is the self. The small knowing binds. Wonder marks the stages of yoga. The self is a dancer who can forget who's dancing. If all of that holds, then the problem isn't missing information. It's a habit of seeing. And a habit of seeing is hard to change by reading alone. Someone can read that the sky is bigger than the keyhole and still look through the keyhole. So the sutra names the means: a teacher. Someone who has seen, and can point. Remember how tradition says this book arrived. Vasugupta didn't invent it. It was shown to him, through a dream and a stone. Even the text comes through someone. Commentators in the tradition widen the word, too. Some read the guru here not only as a person but as grace itself, Shiva's own power to reveal, which can work through a teacher, a line, a moment. On that reading, the grandmother at the slate and the grace behind her aren't two different things. Notice what the line doesn't say. It doesn't say the teacher does the seeing for the student. The guiding hand moves with the child's hand. The child still draws the letter. That's the shape of this sutra: no one gets there alone, and no one gets carried.
screen: `GURU — A TEACHER.` · `UPAYA — THE MEANS.` · `A HABIT OF SEEING.` · `GRACE, THROUGH SOMEONE.` · then, large: `THE TEACHER IS THE WAY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember a hand over your hand. Sit, and let the breath settle. Bring to mind someone who showed you a way. It doesn't have to be a spiritual teacher. A parent who taught you to tie a shoe. A coach. A coworker who walked you through your first week. Let their face come, and the moment: what they showed you, and how. On the out-breath, give them a silent thank-you. If another face comes, welcome it too. If you pray, you can thank Shiva for the teachers who came, and the grace that came through them. The bell holds the time.
Kashmir Shaivism opening, the Shiva Sutras. Today's line: gurur upayah, the teacher is the way.

Your line: Kashmir Shaivism opening, the Shiva Sutras. Today, when someone shows you how to do something, however small, notice it as teaching, and thank them. Day one thousand one hundred forty-three.

howItsDone: Students of Kashmir Shaivism learn the Shiva Sutras from a teacher, line by line, with a commentary, and the tradition treats the teacher's guidance, and grace through the teacher, as part of the path itself.

fork.setup: you've read every line of the Shiva Sutras, and you still look at the world through the keyhole. what does today's sutra name as the means?
fork.reveal: gurur upayah: the teacher is the way. a habit of seeing changes with help from someone who has seen.

what a scholar hears: Shiva Sutras 2.6, gurur upayah, which Kshemaraja's commentary also reads as the grace-bestowing power of Shiva acting as guru.
